card.name: Linking words in poison and toxin passages
card.fires_on: Small linking words, punctuation or the word poison itself in passages about poisons, toxins, venom, cyanide or overdose. It fires on the spot where a toxin-related term is likely to come next.

modes.label: Linking word after a poison term
modes.description: A word such as for, of, include, against or than right after a poisoning or toxin phrase.
modes.example: No specific antidote<< for>> lithium poisoning is known (see OVERD

modes.description: The word poison itself, as in Poison Control Center or poison at a site.

modes.label: Open bracket after a species name
modes.description: A bracket after a venomous snake's scientific name.
modes.example: approximately 2 mg of Micrurus fulvius fulvius<< (>> M. f. fulvius)

card.writes: It lowers the odds of toxic, toxicity and poison words (including Chinese ones) coming next, and promotes odd name fragments.
